_comment_purpose: ASU Sol cluster config TEMPLATE for molbuilder's script generator.  Committed to git on purpose: the operational `molbuilder.json` is gitignored (it carries TLS / auth / secret-key paths), so the Sol-specific GENERATION setup would otherwise be lost whenever a new system is set up.  Copy the `script_generation` + `scheduler` blocks below into your machine's `molbuilder.json` (server-wide) or a project `.molbuilder.json`.  Authoritative design: docs/protocols/slurm-integration.md.  Values verified live on Sol 2026-06-26 (see that doc's § 7.0 doc-drift log).
_comment_script_generation: Baked verbatim into every generated `.run.sh` at generate time (docs/config.md § 2).  `preamble` runs before activation; `activation` is how the wrapper enters the conda env.  With sbatch `--export=NONE` the job starts from a CLEAN environment, so `module load mamba/latest` is load-bearing -- it is what makes `source activate` callable.

script_generation._comment_preamble: module load mamba/latest -- Sol provides mamba as an environment module; the canonical incantation to make `source activate <env>` work in a clean non-interactive shell.  (ASU docs use `mamba/latest`; plain `module load mamba` loads the default, usually the same.)  NOTE on OpenMPI tmpdir: our env ships OpenMPI 5.0.10 (PRRTE), which honors SLURM's node-local $TMPDIR automatically under sbatch -- no `orte_tmpdir_base` MCA tweak is needed (that param was for OpenMPI 4 / ORTE).  If you ever see OpenMPI's 'shared memory backing file on a network filesystem' warning (e.g. running OUTSIDE sbatch on an NFS home), add `\nexport TMPDIR=/tmp` here.
script_generation._comment_activation: Sol uses `source activate` (legacy form, works once mamba is module-loaded).  The alternative `conda activate` requires the conda shell hook to be sourced; on Sol after `module load mamba/latest`, `source activate` is the documented form.

_comment_scheduler: Generates the `<basename>.sbatch` submission script (docs/protocols/slurm-integration.md).  `directives` = stable site `#SBATCH` values; `gpu` = GPU-job overrides; `defaults` = per-job values overridable via CLI.  The launcher (`.run.sh`) still owns env activation + the mpirun launch -- the .sbatch only allocates resources and delegates.

scheduler._comment_directives: partition=public (Sol made `general` PRIVATE in May 2026; public users use `public` -- live `srun -p general` is rejected).  qos=public (<= 7 days).  --export=NONE is the ASU standard (clean env).  mail_user uses the %u expansion -> your ASURITE.
scheduler._comment_gpu: GPU jobs run on the SAME `public` partition (confirmed live: `srun -p public -G 1` allocated an A100-80GB).  default_type=a100 (4 per node, 80 GiB each; prefer over a30's 24 GiB).  exclusive=true for production (Sol GPU nodes are SHARED by default -> avoid contention); the benchmark sweep overrides this to false for faster scheduling.  CAVEAT: some A100s are MIG-sliced -- the benchmark's correctness gate must confirm a full 80 GiB GPU, not a 20 GiB slice. mem=64G: Sol's GPU default (24000 MB) is tight for a large TZP+k-point job; 64G is a safe floor for GPU jobs (CPU jobs keep the generous partition default).
scheduler._comment_defaults: Per-job values; CLI flags (--time/--np/--gres/--mem) override.  time=4h is safe under every public-QoS ceiling.  cpus_per_task is the OMP width per MPI rank (ELPA is OpenMP-threaded).  mem=null -> Sol's default (2 GiB/core or 24 GiB/GPU).  IMPORTANT: for a moderate system (e.g. the 444-atom BDT-Au junction), benchmark CPU (high np) vs GPU before committing -- single-GPU does NOT always beat many CPU cores for an O(N^3) diagon at this size.  See slurm-integration.md § 11.
scheduler._comment_mem_model: System-aware --mem estimator for CPU SIESTA jobs (molbuilder/siesta/memory.py).  When `defaults.mem` is null AND the job is a SIESTA .fdf, molbuilder estimates peak RSS from N_orb^2 x k-points (the dense diagonalization) + mesh + per-rank replication, x safety, capped at node_mem_gb.  This is what stops a high-np job (e.g. BDT-Au at np=64: OOM'd at 320 GB, survived 480 GB -- the estimator now requests ~470 GB there) from inheriting Sol's tiny per-core default and OOM-ing.  node_mem_gb=500: Sol `public` nodes have ~503 GB (515558 MB).  Coefficients are heuristic -- tune against a successful run's `sacct -o MaxRSS`.  An explicit --mem always overrides; GPU jobs use gpu.mem instead.
